newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks extend slide on auction forecast.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks extend slide on auction forecast.

text.p: Mexican stocks extended their midday slump at the close on Tuesday after the market forecast higher increases in primary interest rates, traders and analysts said.

"What hit the market more than anything was the expectation of greater increases in primary interest rates, that's what it moved on today," said Hector Jimenez, an equity analyst at the Inverlat brokerage in Mexico City said.
The leading IPC share index ended down 40.68 points, or 1.06 percent, at 3,804.12. Trading volume was unremarkable at 88.4 million shares.

A Reuters survey of nine money market traders in Mexico City showed they forecast that Banco de Mexico would assign bellwether 28-day Cetes at an average rate of 22.09 percent. This would be an increase of 93 basis points from last week's auction.
Traders had expected a rise of 25-50 basis points in early trade.
"Nonetheless, we believe the IPC is consolidating and will seek to halt its slide at a floor of 3,750 points," Jimenez added.
Analysts said international factors were still weighing down on the bourse.
"The market is still awaiting and we may even stay nervous over the forthcoming Federal Open Market Committee meeting," said Esteban Rojas, deputy head of research at the Arka brokerage.
"What's more, the bourse is still in a waiting period before the U.S. House of Representatives votes on certifying Mexico (as a drugs war ally)," he added.
U.S. House Majority Leader Dick Amery said earlier he expected a resolution on Thursday.

President Clinton decided to certify Mexico's efforts in combatting drugs on February 28, but the House International Relations Committee voted on March 6 to overturn the rating. On the broad market, 99 stocks changed hands, of which declines outnumbered gains 51 to 23.
Telecoms firm Telemex L class was the most heavily traded decliner, off 10 centavos at 16.00 pesos.
Financial group Abaco L shares topped the declines' list Traders said financial stocks in general ended down on predicted interest rate rises that would tend to increase their bad-loans burden.
Retail stock Cifra B class was another prominent slider, which ended off 93 centavos at 11.38 pesos. Dealers said the stock fell after a dividend payment of 25 centavos per share.
Glassmaker Vitro was a leading gainer, which ended up 80 centavos at 22.00 pesos following news Libbey said it would buy a $100 million stake in the firm's tableware business.
